synopsis: The corpus recommends a hybrid “environment factory”: combining methods matters more than selecting one authoring package, and a quarry model can mix plans, surveys, hand-built gaps, asset libraries and hundreds of procedural variants [f3700, f3775, f3774, f15998]. It identifies eleven method families; existing plans and asset libraries are the fastest resources for a broad portfolio, while hybrid multi-source twins have the highest initial integration effort but lower effort per subsequent variant [f3773, f3704, f4279]. Planning estimates remain uncertain: no numeric effort or cost per site was found for any of the eleven families, no independent cost-normalisation study was found, and comparison ratings are relative judgements unless numbers are supplied [f4170, f4171, f4172, f4169]. RoadRunner supports imports, reconstruction and simulator exports, with R2026b the latest release found, but its road-oriented editor needs custom work-site semantics; OpenUSD and Omniverse can represent sites but do not constitute a validation method [f8605, f8606, f9156, f8607, f9168]. Reconstruction is a bottleneck rather than a solved prerequisite: reusable site representations are needed before scenario volume matters, reconstructed RadaRays meshes were too large to clean manually, log-based appearance reconstruction struggles with viewpoint changes, and every captured environment needs a capture date and revision history [f16011, f4964, f16004, f16013].
